newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Tronoh sees boosting stake in Hillgrove.
newsitem.headline: Tronoh sees boosting stake in Hillgrove.

text.p: Tronoh Mines Malaysia Bhd said on Wednesday it was optimistic it would be able to exercise an option to boost its stake in Australia's Hillgrove Gold NL to nearly 56 percent.

"We are quite positive of exercising it unless we have reasons to believe it isn't a good investment," Tronoh chief executive Lim Che Wan told reporters after the company's annual meeting with shareholders.
Tronoh will have to pay 10 Australian cents each, or a gross A$5 million, for the additional 50 million shares, Lim said.
The Malaysian mining company had earlier bought 40 million shares, also at 10 cents each, in Hillgrove between August 1996 and February this year.
"With the new next option, our stake in Hillgrove will just be under 56 percent," said Lim.
"The shares which we bought at 10 (Australian) cents have already doubled to 20 cents. This already means we have recovered our investment," he added.
Lim said another positive factor was the recent confirmation of about 1.6 million tonnes of gold ore under mining rights held by Hillgrove.
"With this confirmation, we hope to produce 230,000 tonnes of gold ore a year for the next seven years, compared to the 60,000 tonnes now," said Lim.
The additional output will convert to higher gold production of around 70,000 equivalent ounces of gold, against the present 14,000 to 15,000 ounces.
"Hillgrove is also working to produce gold bullions to upgrade the current production facility, to a stage where it can be directly sold to end-buyers," said Lim.

Apart from Hillgrove, Tronoh also holds a 29 percent stake in Plutonic Resources Ltd, an Australian gold miner. In 1996, production from Plutonic's gold mines rose 29 percent to 449,811 ounces from 348,704 ounces in 1995.
The contribution from Plutonic helped Tronoh achieve a 5.2 percent rise in group pre-tax profit to 27.8 million ringgit for the year to January 31, 1997.
Lim said Hillgrove was expected to contribute to Tronoh's earnings by December 31, 1998.
